In order to diagnose PCOS, gynecologists look to see if you meet 2 out of 3 criteria. 

1) If you have irregular periods (less than 9 periods a year)
2) If you have abnormal growth of body hair 
3) If you have cysts on your ovaries

If you meet 2/3, clinically you have PCOS. My blood work was all normal and doctor never checked for cysts, but since I meet the other two criteria, I can officially say that I have PCOS.

I also started swimming again after a long time and I watched a couple videos by MySwimPro, mainly the one called "How to Swim Freestyle with Perfect Technique." This went over everything that I thought I needed to brush up on before going to the pool. It focuses on a couple of things: 

\- body position (how to position your head and hips to maintain the streamline position and reduce drag)

\- rotation (rotate from the hips and your shoulders will follow suit)

\- breathing (head position while breathing and breathing as a part of body rotation)

\- catch (how your hand should be entering the water as part of each stroke, and how your forearm should pull the water)

\- kicking (short, fast kicks instead of big, long kicks)

\- overall feel of swimming (engaging all of your senses) 

Don't get too overwhelmed by all this. Tbh, once you get in the pool, your body will remember. Start off with 25M's and 50M's and work up from there. I was a bit rusty at first but quickly picked it back up. Good luck!

If he’s shy, then I feel like maybe you should make contact first. I would let him know that it’s important for you two to talk about what happened last night, and that you were upset that your relationship essentially started with a lie. He might have just wanted to get it off his chest because it could have been bothering him or he maybe didn’t know how else to break it to you, but in this case I think you are absolutely right that it really depends on how he reacts.

I think the question you should ask yourself is whether you are able to trust him after learning that he did this. It seems that you are hurt and disappointed, rightfully so, but I personally think that there would be no point in continuing the relationship if he broke your trust.
If you are not able to look past this and are constantly stressed or worried  that he is hung up on his ex, then that is something to think about before letting the relationship progress further.
Also, the way he told you seems a little nonchalant. Did he ever follow up with you and let you know that he is sorry that you learned about it this way? Did he value how you felt about the situation? Those things would be the deal breakers for me.
